utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom and to those listening to these proceedings. Are there any procedural matters? Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone. There is one preliminary matter, Mr. President. I need to go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you have already testified in this trial. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony many months ago still applies. Today, you are testifying about another subject matter. Mr. Vanderpuye will be putting questions to you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good afternoon again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I wanted to show you some video footage that the Prosecution has tendered in this case because I'd like you to provide the Trial Chamber, if you could, with some information relevant to the question of the authenticity of this video footage. The first video I'd like to show you is from 19 July, which concerns the Jela Restaurant, and I'd like to show it to you first, and then you can perhaps give us a little bit of information concerning its provenance. It's P740, and I think we can start at just about the beginning of the footage at 00, and we'll play it through 2 minutes, 44 seconds or so. So let's take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just stop the footage right now at 1:18.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us who this individual is with the moustache?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This individual is Mr. Indjic from the VRS. I forgot his first name. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could it be Boban Indjic? If you don't remember, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so he's Boban Indjic. It should be something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you should avoid leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc -- or perhaps you're asking the witness about the basis of his knowledge about this, the identity of this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, I was just about to. I was going to ask him first to identify the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the location that we see here in the video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Jela Restaurant in Han Kram, near Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a footage, and we later on see when the agreement was signed between the General Mladic, representing the VRS on one side, and the UNPROFOR members, General Smith. And we know that this took place from different sources. One of those would be witnesses who are present at this meeting and who testified here in this trial, and we interviewed them before. There are then several documents, in particular this agreement which was signed there, and from these sources we can conclude this is Jela Restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Have you been to this restaurant yourself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that location, but at the time when I was there, the building was not there anymore. It's destroyed right now. So I haven't entered the actual building, but I was at that spot, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me play a little bit more of the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, I have a question for you, Mr. Janc. Were you there in this restaurant? First, that's the question, first question. The second question: How can you tell, by looking at this room in which this gentleman is standing, that this is the Jela Restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think I've answered part of your question and that I was not inside this restaurant, because at the time when I was there, for my first time, that was in 2006, the building was not there anymore, so I couldn't enter it. That this is going on in this restaurant I can tell from the statements which were taken from the witnesses which are present in this restaurant. Particularly I'm referring here to Mr. David Wood, who I interviewed in London back then, I think, in 2007 or 2008, and he identified this building as being -- and this room as being the Jela Restaurant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put a follow-up question. In which way did you know -- or did you get information about the identity of the person of Mr. Indjic ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would say through same sources. I think, also, David Wood told us about him, and he was very often present at that time in these meetings, attending these meetings with UNPROFOR, because he was interpreting for -- from B/C/S into English and from English into B/C/S for the VRS. So from these sources we know, basically from the sources we interviewed, that this is this individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Let's just play this on through 2 minutes and 43 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us -- I'm sorry, we stopped at 1 minute, 35 seconds again. Can you tell us who we have in the frame?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I will try to remember, because I don't see the picture on the screen anymore. Far right, I think it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Don't you have the picture in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Court Usher should assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ah, now it is. Thank you. It was different button. So, yes, let me start maybe from the left-hand side. This is General Ratko Mladic, and next to him is General Rupert Smith, and the last one on the right-hand side we can see is Colonel Baxter from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We can play it through a little bit, and then I'd like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We've stopped it at 2 minutes, 41.9 seconds. I'd like to show you, if I could, Mr. Janc, P1977.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, have you seen this document before, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it is, what it's about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an UNPROFOR report, I think, regarding this meeting at Jela Restaurant on 19th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does it correspond to the video footage that we've seen concerning the 19 July meeting between General Smith and General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to go to the next page, if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I wouldn't want to take up the Prosecutor's time, but this video footage was already identified when Mr. Rupert Smith was here and his associates, and I don't know why do we have to do it again, although I have no complaints about it being tendered and accepted into evidence. And, secondly, there is no translation. I don't know what's being discussed here. I don't speak English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, both the document -- the video and this document are already in evidence, and we have seen the video. It's up to the Prosecution to decide. And what about the translation, Mr. Vanderpuye? Now I see it. We have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if there's no objection to the video evidence being received -- I understood that it was MFI'd, but if it's otherwise admitted in evidence and there's no objection to it, then I think there is not much need to authenticate it. In any event, I will have Mr. Janc briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just was informed by the Registrar that you're right, the video is MFI'd and not admitted into evidence yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did you have an opportunity to review this document? As you can see from the title, it's from Lieutenant-Colonel Baxter, and it concerns a meeting -- it's dated July 19, 1995, and concerns a meeting between General Smith and General Mladic. Did you consult this in evaluating the provenance of the video footage that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can see here, at the end of paragraph 1, a reference to -- well, the sentence reads that: "General Mladic was accompanied by General Tolimir and Lieutenant-Colonel Indic." Can you tell us about that in relation to the footage that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. As we have seen and identified Lieutenant-Colonel Indjic on the video before, and also from the video we could see the face of General Tolimir also being present before the meeting, before the agreement has been signed, and he was there. And also from the comments made later on by General Mladic during the meeting itself, when the agreement was signed, Mladic has referred to him, to General Tolimir, several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, we should see the sequence of the video again where we can see Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As indicated by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to tell who this individual is? We're at 00:24.6.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we have a little bit better picture before this frame, a little bit -- we can see a little bit more of him. And also he was identified by David Wood during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Identified by David Wood during the interview that you conducted with him?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you seen other photographs of General Tolimir from this time-frame?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not only photographs. We have also other videos from this time -- from that time, about General Tolimir being present at different meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We can roll on a little bit further to see what General Mladic says about General Tolimir. And we'll have to go to the part where General Mladic and General Smith are together, so that's -- yeah, this is probably a good place to start. That's at 1 minute, 26 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here, we've stopped at 2 minutes -- pretty much 2 minutes even, and we see General Mladic saying: "I'll go, but General Tolimir will stay here."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that what you were referring to previously in response to the questions from the Bench?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not only this, because this is only a segment of the entire video and also the segment of this meeting itself. We have a much longer portion of this meeting on the tape itself, and several times -- at least one or two more times during this meeting General Mladic is referring to General Tolimir. At one point, he refers to him just as "Toso." As we know, that was his nickname at that time, so -- but also as "General Tolimir."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. President, I would like to tender this video footage to be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received as P740.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show you another video, Mr. Janc. That one is P2231. We're right at the beginning of this frame. It's 00:14.9. And before I play it: Can you tell us, first of all, do you recognise this scene?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's the outside of this same Jela Restaurant, and this is now on 20 of July, 1995, one day after that one we see -- we just saw. And this is actually the farewell ceremony or party for General Milenko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to play you some of this footage and then I'll ask you some questions about it. So let's play this through 1 minute and 52 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please stop here. Mr. Gajic wants to comment something. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to all. Mr. President, we are not able to hear anything. We don't have any sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I agree, we don't hear anything, that's right. We only see the subtitles.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I agree. We'll try and work that out. There is sound, for sure, on this segment of the video, so I think we have just a technical problem to work out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I hear something now. I wonder if you can hear it. We may have to turn the headphones up somewhat, but I can hear the sound now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, we hear it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Shall we try again, then? We'll start right at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we should do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's play it. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We've stopped it now at 1:14.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us who the individual is in the middle -- just about the middle of this frame?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is General Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he identified himself during this trial, and also I met him before, several times, or at least two times before, so I can confirm that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We've now stopped it at 1:32.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the individual is with the hand on his chest or abdomen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is General Milenko Zivanovic, up until that time the commander of Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this individual, I know that that's him from statements I've read and from -- of different individuals who identified him who were shown the photograph of him. And also he was interviewed not by me, but by the other members of the OTP, and from that interview he identified himself as well. And he was one of the sources who gave us this video during that interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we don't have anything against admitting anything, but Mr. Vanderpuye could ask Mr. Janc does he know any other persons in this footage and who is who, because this is recognition on the basis of the film, not on the basis of experience or knowledge. I don't know why this is being done. Thank you. We are putting the witness and the Prosecutor in an uncomfortable position, as well as the Trial Chamber, to accept hearsay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what the basis of the objection is. It seems that the witness has identified General Zivanovic in connection with General Zivanovic's own statement, among other sources, so as to testify about the provenance of the footage that we see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, of course it's a problem. The witness was not present on the spot when this video was taken, so that we must get clear and precise information about the specific source, with whom he discussed the video, who was the person who identified specific the people depicted in the video. So that it can't be enough to say, He was interviewed by an investigator of the OTP. We need a bit more specific answers. Judge Nyambe wants to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Vanderpuye, just to add on to what the Presiding Judge has said, you had the opportunity to produce this video footage through -- I may not be able to pronounce the name, but the deputy commander to General Mladic, who is shown in the footage, who was a witness here just a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and I believe the footage was shown to him during the course of his testimony. I understand that the footage was marked for identification in relation to that, which I'm not sure why. If he identified himself on the footage itself, I'm not sure why it was marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, and I was informed by the Registrar, it was marked for identification not because the people were not identified by the witness, Milovanovic, but the transcript and the translation of the transcript was not produced at that time. And I think this is now available. We saw the subtitles, and I would like to ask you if we have a full translation of the subtitles in both languages. That was the reason we only marked it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see, Mr. President. I think we do, and if you'll bear with me, I can verify that for you. In addition, I do have and I was intending to present the Trial Chamber with the statement of General Milovanovic, who was depicted in this footage - actually, in the frame that we have before us right now - in which he identifies himself and he identifies this meeting that actually took place on the 20th, which I think obviously is of relevance to the authenticity of the video footage, in addition to General Milovanovic's identification of himself as having been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I remember correctly, and I think it would be good for all of us to be reminded at this time, specifically that this part was not shown to Witness Milovanovic when he testified here, only the sections from the restaurant and, if I remember correctly, near a chopper that is seen here in the footage considerably later, I belive. So what we're looking at now, I think we did not see before, when General Milovanovic was here. Only a few seconds were played to him of this particular segment, perhaps a minute or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's my recollection as well, but I think that the video footage is continuous. And so to the extent that we have an individual who identifies himself as being at a meeting in one part of the footage, and the continuity of that footage shows other parts of that meeting, it seems to me that having identified himself at the beginning part of the video-tape bears on the authenticity or the provenance of the entirety of the tape, particularly since he confirmed that he was at this going-away, he also confirmed that General Mladic was at the going-away, and I believe he also confirmed some of the substance of what the gathering was about. And I think that the video footage, in its entirety, or at least the parts I intend to show, substantiate that. And that's the basis of the relevance of showing these other parts of the footage as well as introducing other components which support its authenticity and reliability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That part of the video we are discussing about was shown to the witness Manojlo Milovanovic on the 18th of May, 2011, and the Chamber decided already to receive it as an exhibit, but only mark it until we have received the translation and the transcript. That's all. And therefore I'm not sure if it's really necessary to identify those people to be shown on the video who are already identified by an eye-witness who took part in this meeting; for instance, Witness Milovanovic. He testified about the helicopter flight, the arrival of General Mladic, in other parts of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. President. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And, again, please help us and tell us if the transcript and the translation is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think there's not a translation available. As you know, the video footage itself is in B/C/S, so I think Mr. Gajic can understand that. It is subtitled, so there's not an English transcription of it. But, clearly, if that will assist the Court, we'll get that done. I don't think the entirety of the video is subtitled. A good portion of it is, and that's what I intended to show the Trial Chamber. And if Mr. Gajic has an objection to the subtitles, as they compare to the B/C/S audio, I'm sure that he will let us know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Once again, this is the only matter we should discuss with this video, because there was no doubt that this one is an authentic document. And, in fact, we decided on the admission of this document already. So I would kindly ask you to consider if it is necessary to ask this witness to identify people present in addition to the identification of some people who have been present on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll do my best to avoid that. I'm not sure exactly who's identified whom in all of this footage, because we have quite a bit of footage, but I'll do my best to avoid that, if at all possible. There is one other individual, though, I did want him to try and identify, whom I'm not sure has been identified thus far, so I'd like to ask him about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you see this individual who is behind General Zivanovic to his left? That would be over his left shoulder. That would be to the right on the frame in front of us.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this one, but it's not -- the picture is not clear, so I can't say anything right now who that might be.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we play it a little bit from this point forward, let us know if you're able to do that. We're at 1:32.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to identify that individual?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, this is General Momir Talic. He was at that time the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was indictee of this Tribunal. That's one source. I think also during this video footage he is referred several times as General Momir Talic. And also he gives a pistol to General Zivanovic at one point in time during this ceremony, inside the -- inside the restaurant, and we have a kind of a document from him, from General Talic, regarding this pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Is he mentioned at all during the course of the interview that was conducted with General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is, indeed. So he's also mentioned in his interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In what context?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in context of this, of getting a pistol from him, and that's when we were also provided with the document from General Zivanovic about this pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's play forward a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should first state the time when you have stopped it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We're at 1:38.6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you are referring to the person at the right side of the frame; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: You said you have had occasion to -- no, no, no, that's not what you're saying. Sorry. And I'll rephrase my question. Have you had occasion to meet General Momir Talic face to face, yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, because he passed away many years ago, I think in 1996, 1997, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: So your knowledge of him is from other sources, secondary sources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The secondary source, in terms of your identification of Momir Talic, did that come from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was that a photograph of him as a suspect or an indictee of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's play forward here from 1:38.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually, we can play forward. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us where these gentlemen are? We're stopped, I'm sorry, at 1:55.1. Where is this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now they are inside the Jela Restaurant. Where exactly, which room, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is to go forward to 19:34.11. I think that's right. And we can play it forward from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We've stopped at 21:18.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here we see -- well, you tell us. Tell us if you agree that this is General Mladic in this frame. Yes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you receive any information or did you learn any information concerning General Mladic's arrival here by helicopter, as we see in the footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. In what sense do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you read anything that said that he arrived there or hear any testimony in this case, concerning this meeting, indicating that General Mladic arrived by helicopter?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General Mladic was talking about it, and I think also General Milovanovic during his interview, when he was interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to play you another part of this video footage, starting at 23:39.4. And before I play it, let me ask you this: Did you have any information about what transpired during this particular gathering on the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's play the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We've stopped at 33:54.3. And I'd like to play for you, Mr. Janc, starting at 42:48.66. We can play it now from 42:48.0.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we stopped at 44:10.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we can see General Zivanovic is holding up a gun, Mr. Janc, and you can see next to him the individual who you identified previously as Momir Talic. Is this the portion you referred to when you spoke about Momir Talic giving Zivanovic, General Zivanovic, a gun?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you find that in the statement of General Zivanovic when you read it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's play this footage through 47:13.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. We've stopped it at 47:02.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can see from this footage, Mr. Janc, that it's somewhat of a festive occasion. Can you tell us, or remind us, rather, when this occurred relative to the executions that occurred at the Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was four days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And during the course of this, we could see that General Mladic made some comments concerning Gorazde and Bihac. Can you just remind us of what those areas were back then in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gorazde was enclave. For Bihac, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what about Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time still, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us or just remind us when this celebration occurred relative to the executions at Bisina?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is three day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At this point in time, I would like to state that the last part of the video we have seen was not subtitled. We only heard some parts of the speech and other voices. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. With all due respect, I have to emphasise that this witness was called in order to identify the footage, rather than providing any information or arguments to the Prosecution concerning something that happened later. So I would ask that this be taken into account. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You are correct, the last part of the transcript -- I'm not sure where it cut out, but somewhere around 40 minutes the subtitles did end. I'd like to show the witness 65 ter 2783. This is the OTP statement of General Zivanovic from 2001. We'll have to go to page 17 in the English and page 12 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I just want to refer you to the last two paragraphs in the English, and here you can see General Zivanovic, during the course of this interview, is presenting a pistol. He says: "I never fired a bullet." And read -- and he says that it reads -- the description reads: "To the commander of the Drina Corps, General M. Zivanovic." Then it says: "1 KK, the 1st Krajina Corps, 12th, 7 July -- the 12th, 1995." He says: "This gun -- this -- the gun and the document are presented ..." And the transcript reads that it's indiscernible. "... when they would be ... where Talic was also present. I now have a cassette which explains a lot, at the ceremony of my departure on July the 20th ..." And then it says. "... at Motel Jela on Romanija." Is that what you were referring to previously in respect of this video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here it's referred to as the Motel Jela. Is that the same as the location that we've seen in this footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely it is, but I'm not sure why general was referring here to motel rather than to a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks very much, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: As stated in the transcript, we are looking at the statement of General Zivanovic. Is it my understanding that he has since died? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. General Zivanovic is still alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But General Momir Talic, who gave a pistol to General Zivanovic, he passed away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. In any event, my next question is: Did you -- are you the one who took this statement from the person who gave it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it wasn't me. It was my colleague, Investigator Allistair Graham, and this was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I know that this video is still MFI'd, pending the appropriate translations, and we'll see to it that the Trial Chamber is provided with that. Other than that condition, I would propose to admit it. I would like to show the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was already decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have another question, for a better understanding. We see, in the B/C/S version of the statement given by General Zivanovic to the OTP, we see there the abbreviation "AG," that seems to be Mr. Graham; and the abbreviation "MZ," that seems to be the witness, Zivanovic. What about the others? "PMC," who is that? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, Your Honour. This one is referring to Peter McCloskey, who was also present during this interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye, carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think if we go to the very first page we might be able to see all of this. That may be helpful to the Trial Chamber. Here, we can see who are the parties that are present, and it indicates that Allistair Graham is there, Senior Trial Attorney Peter McCloskey is there, General Milenko Zivanovic is there, and then there's also an interpreter there by the name of Miljena Petkovic [phoen], and also Mirka Zivanovic, who is General Zivanovic's wife. And the date is indicated as 30th of October, 2001. I won't be tendering this particular document. I think it's sufficient that it's shown to the Trial Chamber. But I would like to show the witness another video footage which I have here as P740. I just want to show you this footage from the same video-tape as the 19 July Jela Restaurant meeting in Han Kram. This, you can see, indicates UN check-point Boksanica, 24 July 1995, and it's pretty short. We'll play it through to -- well, we're at 35:32, and we'll play it through 35:41, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us who is the individual here in the blue suit in this video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell who the person is to the left of General Tolimir, maybe not in this frame, but have you seen this footage before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us who the individual is to the left -- to General Tolimir's right, that is, to the left on this frame?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So to his right or to our left-hand side is the person who we can see only half of it. This is commander of the Rogatica Brigade, Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was identified several times from different witnesses showing -- who were shown this video or similar videos from this point and time, and they identified him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First, we stopped at 35:41.7. Secondly, I would like to ask you: What is the source of your identification of the man in the blue jacket?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This individual and all other individuals were also identified by Mr. Hamdija Torlak, I think, also when he testified here for this trial and exactly this footage was shown to him. And he explained in detail who these individuals are there and when exactly this took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So as not to waste more time about this, can we please show the footage, a moving image, so that we could find out how this meeting came to take place and whether this has been edited or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, one simple question: Do you identify the man in the blue jacket as the person present here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's the same person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you are referring to the testimony of Mr. Torlak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. And also we can see this same individual, General Tolimir, on other footages and other videos from this same time-frame period, and I can confirm this is the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I didn't put it on the record, we've stopped at 35:41.7, and I'd like to play it through to 36:11.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We saw that at a certain point this footage became less clear than it was originally, and I would like, if you could, to provide the Trial Chamber with some indication about the source of this video footage.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This segment that we have just seen is taken from the documentary on Avdo Palic's story, which the OTP obtained in 2000, and this segment was part of this documentary. And why the certain -- at a certain moment the footage was changed, it's just because on that documentary the camera is actually taking picture of the television, where the footage is playing, and at one point the picture becomes less clear. So that's why we can also see, here, that difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does that mean that the footage that we see from 35:33.50, or about where we started initially, between that and the end, where we've stopped now at 36:12, that that footage is not continuous, it's been edited?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know if the OTP has made any efforts to identify the source of the video footage that we see here and, in particular, the video footage you say is shot of a television showing these events?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we tried to obtain this footage also from the other sources. And because this was our first source -- the Avdo Palic's documentary was our first source from whom we obtained this video, and we contacted the producer or director of this documentary in order to get the video from him, and he referred us to the BH authorities because, according to him, he was not in possession of this video. And during my investigation, we have asked the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina if they can provide us with video of this same event, and, indeed, just recently they sent us a footage -- a longer footage of the events which occurred around Zepa at that time, and one segment of this bigger footage also included this same segment from 24 of July. Also, there is a third source which I actually obtained from publicly-available YouTube. So there is a third one which we can also get from that public-available source. So it's not the only source we have. So we have confirmed this video, this footage, from other sources as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would have some questions for the witness, but we should do that and continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need the break now, and we will resume quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I would like to ask you to bear in mind the time you are spending with this witness. You indicated two hours. And when we look into the witness summary you provided to the Chamber, I think the most important thing is to identify not the persons depicted in the videos, but the source. And just before the break, Mr. Janc told us something about different types of videos obtained from different sources. This is, in fact, the gist of the testimony of this witness at this stage in the trial. We should avoid just to see all the documents or the videos again which are already in evidence and we discussed it earlier. They are only marked for identification until we receive the transcript and the translation. So please focus on the specific questions you wanted to put to the witness, especially as he was not an eye-witness of the events depicted in these videos, and we have had some of the persons depicted there as witnesses in the Tribunal, as Mr. Torlak, Mr. Milovanovic, and others. Please go ahead, and I would like to ask you to discuss a bit more the sources of these three types of the video we have seen before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. That's exactly where I was headed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you indicated that efforts were made to contact BH authorities with respect to this footage that we've just seen, and that's the 24th July Boksanica footage, P740. I'd like to show you 65 ter 7390.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: While that's loading up -- okay. This is a document that was not part of the original 65 ter list. It was received by the OTP in March. It's dated 11 March 2011, Mr. President, and I'd like to add it to the 65 ter list because I think it responds directly to the issues you're concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This relates to the video I was discussing before which was provided to us, as you can see here, in March 2011 from the State Investigative and Protection Agency of the BiH. And they obtained it from the BiH Radio/Television, as you will see from the following pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On this first page, it indicates that it responds to a request for all video footage relating to Zepa in July 1995. Is that, in fact, what was requested?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to the material that was received, can you tell us what that material was? What did it contain?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a compilation of the footages which were broadcasted at the time regarding Zepa events and what the BiH Radio and Television was able to identify and found in their archives, and that's what they provided to the State Investigative and Protective Agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I show you the next page, please, of this document. Can you tell us what this is? Have you seen it before and can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen this before. And this is what I was referring to, a letter from the Radio and Television of Bosnia and Herzegovina which was provided along with the videos to the BiH state authorities. I mean SIPA.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this a list of the material that was received or the programmes or footage that was received by the OTP from the B&H authorities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7390 shall be assigned Exhibit P2239. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to also add to the 65 ter list 65 ter 7389. This is the video footage that was received by the OTP as per this -- as per this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add it to the 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And we'll need to play this from about 20 seconds. It seems about right. I'm sorry, 20 minutes. 20 minutes. I think that's right, 20 minutes. Okay, let's see if this is right. We can play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, let me just ask: Have you seen this footage before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And does it correspond to the footage that we previously saw in Exhibit P740?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I apologise to the Court. We don't have subtitles for this, so we don't have a translation for you. But let's play it through anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you able to compare this footage to the footage that was in -- I'm sorry, we've stopped at 20:30.7. Were you able to compare this footage to the footage that we saw earlier in P740?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does it -- is it the same footage or is it footage of the same event, perhaps from a different angle or something like that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same event and it is the same camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that you were able to locate this -- the footage of this event, you said, through publicly-available sources. I think you mentioned YouTube.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you able to compare that footage to the footage both in P740 and to this footage, which is 65 ter 7389 for the moment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and they are all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Are they of the same event or are they the same, in other words, shot by the same camera, as opposed to shot from a different angle or something like this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same event and the same camera, from the same angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender 65 ter 7389.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification until we see and we receive the transcript and the translation. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. Because there was mention of editing during the examination of this witness, I would like to know whether the OTP handed this in for an expertise to determine what was edited and what was not. Maybe it would be better to have it admitted only after an expertise has been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The statement of Mr. Janc about editing a video was made in relation to the previous document, P740, and not in relation to this one we just have received. In addition, you may deal with that in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7389 shall be assigned Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No. Now the Registrar has the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With your leave, Your Honours, 65 ter document 7389 shall be assigned Exhibit P2240, marked for identification, pending translation and transcription. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. I cannot ask either the witness or the Prosecutor about why would this be admitted or not. I'm asking you: Is it true that we are admitting all documents, regardless of the fact whether they may have been tampered with during editing or not? Is it all right to admit something that was edited as a credible piece of evidence, because this witness here is to help us with the credibility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber has ruled on that. We have already marked that for identification. And, again, the editing question was in relation to another document, not to this one. And you may ask the witness about the editing process with the other document, P740. No problem with that. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I would like to add: This is exactly the purpose of cross-examination. You have received all the material, you have the witness summary, and this is the issue Mr. Vanderpuye is dealing with. And this is now, then, the purpose of your cross-examination. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to show the witness another video-clip. It's 65 ter 5507. I think we'll need to go into private session for this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We're in -- I've asked to be in private session, Mr. President, because this video-clip is untitled -- an un-subtitled version of P2228. I think that was used in the -- during the course of General Milovanovic's testimony, and some issue arose with respect to the status of the exhibit, which has not yet been resolved. And so I thought, out of an abundance of caution, I should show this clip, because it's part of that same material, in private session. I just want to start out at, I think it should be 49:21 on this clip, and then I will play it through just for a few seconds and then switch to the subtitled version so the Trial Chamber can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you see, first of all, the frame that's in e-court now, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are you able to identify, just from this frame, what this location is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an area south from Crna Rijeka, near Potplanje and Planje area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how were you able to make that determination?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When listening the video itself, from the content, you can conclude what the participants of this conversation are talking about, and exactly they are referring to some villages which are underneath this area, and they are referring to the villages as Planje and Potplanje. And when we obtained this video, the OTP has made an effort to try to identify this location, where exactly this is. And my colleague, Investigator Tomasz Blaszczyk, was going on the field, and he was able to find this location, and he took some picture of it and then took the GPS readings, and he was able to confirm that this is, indeed, that location; not only based on this photo, what we can see on the screen, but we'll have a little bit more area visible on the video itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We can play this through just for a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, it would be helpful, for a better understanding of what we are going to see, if you could, with the witness, elaborate a little bit more about the source of this video, where he got it from, and, yeah, including the question of editing. That would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First of all, can you tell us what the source of this video is, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The OTP obtained this video -- or actually received on 24 of August, 2009, from the authorities of the Republic of Canada. And during the interrogation of their citizen, Mr. Milan Lesic, at the beginning of August of that year, they seized this particular video from him. And this individual is the representative of Serb community in Canada, and I've been discussing -- actually, testifying about this video and another video which was also provided by him to the authorities of the -- Canada on the same day when I testified about the meeting in -- on 16 of July in Belgrade with Mladic and other persons present and on 17 of July. That was during my last testimony. And from the same source, on the same date, we also obtained this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think we might as well explore this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could show the witness, please, 65 ter 6580. That's under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't believe we have a translation of this document. I'll read a bit of it into the record so that General Tolimir can have some acquaintance with what it is. It's dated 21 August 2009. It's -- the stationary, or letterhead, indicates "Department of Justice, Canada, Ontario Regional Office," and it is directed to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY, and it refers to: "Dear Mr. Piekos."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us who that is, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This individual is the investigator of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then it says: "Regarding Lesic, Milan, court file number ...," and it says "Crim Mot F," and then it gives a number, "... witness evidence hearing 6th and 7th August, 2009, Superior Court of Justice (Central West Region - Brampton)." And the letter indicates as follows: "Please find enclosed a certified copy of the sending-abroad order dated August 20, 2009, signed by the Honourable Senior Regional Madam Justice F. Van Melle of the Superior Court of Justice (Central West Region - Brampton)." And then it says in the next paragraph: "... find enclosed a copy of the report of the Honourable ... Justice ... Van Melle ..." And it says: "Attached to the report is a copy of the exhibit list containing four pages of documented exhibits. "Also find enclosed are various-sized envelopes containing actual exhibits corresponding to the exhibit list which were all produced by Mr. Milan Lesic during his testimony heard ... on August 6th and 7, 2009, before ... Justice ... Van Melle."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you explain why this was put under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can. I'm just about to go to the next page of it, and I think that explains it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we go to the next page of this document, we'll see the sending-abroad order. I'm sorry, the page after that. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here, you can -- this is entitled -- for the benefit of General Tolimir, it's entitled "Superior Court of Justice (Central West Region), and it says: "In the matter of an application pursuant to Section 20 of the Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Act for sending-abroad order regarding the examination of a witness pursuant to Section 18(2)(a) of the Act, and in the matter of a request for assistance from the United Nations International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia." Essentially, this, in paragraph 1, orders that all original exhibits filed during the examination of Milan Lesic on 6th and 7th 2009 [sic], which are described in the attached list, be sent forthwith to the ICTY OTP. That's in paragraph 1. And if we go to two pages up to 65 -- to ERN ending 19, this, hopefully, is responsive to Your Honour's question, and this, in paragraph 7, reads that: "The Court further orders that the OTP not provide any of the items provided by Milan Lesic to third parties or publish or distribute those items in any fashion, except for the purposes of conducting prosecutions before the ICTY and in providing disclosure in the course of those prosecutions, and for the purpose of assisting other law enforcement agencies in the investigation or prosecution of war crimes or crimes against humanity in the former Yugoslavia." Essentially, this is the basis upon which the documents were furnished to the OTP and explains the nature of the restriction with respect to their use in open session. There is some question about the scope of the restriction, but in an abundance of caution at this point, we think it's appropriate to proceed in a private session. If we go to ERN ending 21, page 7 in e-court, we will see the facsimile cover sheet which concerns the transmission of the exhibit list, and you can see here it's dated 14 August 2008, and it comprises some four pages. If we go to the next page, page 8, we'll see the list of exhibits. On this page, we see photos and so on. We'll see on the last -- I'm sorry, not the last page, but ERN ending 24, page 10, if we focus on item 4, we'll see a VHS tape, and it says "August 1994." Can you tell us about that, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is actually the tape, a segment of which we will be just watching in a few minutes, and on this tape, actually, this segment was also part of -- and it's -- on the actual tape, it's a label, "August 1994." And from the stamp on the video itself, you can see that it is dated 15 of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think we can go back to that. We can go back to 65 ter 5507, and we'll just play it briefly, as this is not subtitled, and then we'll go to the subtitled version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we can see what you indicated, the date of August 15, 1994. And, once again, is this the footage that was received by the OTP pursuant to this sending-abroad order?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's play it through just a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we can see we go from this scene immediately to what appears to be the inside of the car. Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First we have seen the scene from outside, from the area, and you could hear the voice of Milan Lesic and General Ratko Mladic. And now they are both inside the car, driving along the road and discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I'd like to do is play you the subtitled portion of this footage, and that's going to come from P2228, which I understand was marked for identification during the course of General Milovanovic's testimony for the reasons that I think were indicated concerning its status as protected, so to speak. And we'll start this right at the beginning of the footage and play it through all the way. It's about 10 minutes long.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We've stopped at 10:46.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask a couple of questions, Mr. Janc. Were you able to identify this route that we see that the car is taking on this -- in this footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were able to identify this route, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you, very briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First I'd like to tender this, if I may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's not enough to say, We were able to identify this route. Could you explain that, please? Which route is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we will be -- I will mark the route on the map. And this route was identified by my colleague, Investigator Tomasz Blaszczyk, when he was on a mission, one of his missions down in the area. So it is a route going down from -- close to Crna Rijeka down to Potplanje and towards the Zepa enclave, and I will mark the exact route on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Have you been there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on part of this route, yes. I was there once, but not in the entire route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I have a question for you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Your witness on the stand now says: "My colleague, Investigator Tomasz ... one of his missions down in the area." Indicating that really this is something in the knowledge of the investigator that he refers to. Why wasn't this produced through that investigator?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's a good question, and I can offer the following explanation: We decided that it would be most appropriate, since Mr. Janc is dealing with this video footage, and quite a large amount of the OTP's video footage, that it would be more efficient to have Mr. Janc discuss that footage. He discussed previous footage received from the -- are we in open session now? We're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We're still in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. He received this material and has testified about footage that was provided from the same source that we see in this particular instance, pursuant to his prior testimony about video footage that comprised part of the trial video and other materials before the Trial Chamber, and so we thought that it would be a more efficient way to present the evidence to have Mr. Janc talk about all of those videos. The fact that it's within the knowledge of Mr. Blaszczyk as well I don't think is necessarily anything that detracts from the reliability of the information that Mr. Janc brings to the Trial Chamber, except for the fact that it's second-hand, it's not first-hand. The rules of evidence in this Tribunal provide for the admission or admissibility of second-hand information. There's simply no rule against the admission of hearsay evidence, and that comes in, in a variety of forms. It comes in a variety of forms in terms of documents, video footage, even testimonial evidence. So I don't know, necessarily, that it's fundamentally a lesser standard of evidence than any other evidence that comes before the Trial Chamber. So I think -- I think, under Rule 89 -- I think it's 89(C), it would be appropriate for the Trial Chamber to receive it, even though Investigator Janc has direct knowledge of having driven the route. But, remember, even though Investigator Janc directly drove the route, Investigator Janc didn't shoot the video, and he's relying on what he sees in the video, or whoever shot the video, or however the video was shot, to bring to you that information in any event. So no matter how you toss it up, unless it's the person that's riding in the car, i.e., General Mladic or Milan Lesic, it is second-hand information in any event. So I don't think that the fact that it's Investigator Janc or it's Investigator Blaszczyk really makes much of a difference in terms of the provenance or the reliability of the information for the Trial Chamber. In addition to that, the Trial Chamber has the video itself, and so I think the Trial Chamber is in a position to compare what's in the video to what Mr. Janc represents is the route or what Mr. Blaszczyk would have represented was the route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: To the extent that you want to tell the Chamber, through this witness, the route of -- the route that was taken, you don't think a person who has been on that route is a better witness for you than the one who hasn't been?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do think that person is a better witness for me, but I don't think that it's a necessary witness for me. And I think there's a difference between that. I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so that, to me, is a question of the weight to be attributed to the evidence, but the evidence in this case is the video. The principal evidence that we offer to the Trial Chamber is the video itself. So I think that Mr. Janc's testimony concerning the route is helpful to the Trial Chamber to assess the video, although I don't think it's necessary to the Trial Chamber to assess the video, because the video is what it is. It speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you are tendering the document P2228 which was previously marked for identification. I take it this document contains four different videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It does, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have seen two of them, one today and one with the witness Milovanovic. If I'm not mistaken, that was the New Year's celebration.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think that's right, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why is it one document that makes it quite difficult to deal with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's a very good question. I think, in the end, it's going to form part of a compilation video, and that's the reason why it's on one document for the moment. You're right, it does complicate things somewhat. There is one other segment of the video that I wanted to play to Mr. Janc, but it still leaves another segment of the video without his testimony, and so I understand the Court's concern. I don't know that there's a way to admit it in parts or pieces of it, which perhaps might be the most appropriate way to do it. But, in any event, I think that whatever hasn't been shown to the Trial Chamber will be shown to the Trial Chamber either now or at some other point, and so maybe it's appropriate to leave it marked for identification until that happens. But, in any event, I do have one other segment on this video, on this document, that I would like to show the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, we have seen now that part which is under seal, according to the conditions set up by the Canadian authorities, and, therefore, we are still in private session. I think it is a good proposal to postpone a decision about the final admission of the evidence after we have seen the other portions. Are they also under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: They are not, Mr. President, and we can go into open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We go into a public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If it would be helpful to the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Please hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If it would be helpful to the Trial Chamber, I would like to have Mr. Janc detail the route that we've just seen on the video footage, but only if it's helpful. If it's not, otherwise, then there's certainly no problem in moving on to the next segment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is your witness. You should decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then I would like to show it to him, please. And it's - just a moment - P104, and I think it might be helpful to go to Map 10. Probably -- Mr. Janc will probably need the assistance of the Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Not with a hard copy, but with the screen. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we'll need to go to page 12 in e-court. I think we probably don't need the translation, if there is one, and we can just put it on one screen. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this a helpful map for you, Mr. Janc? And let us know if we should blow it up or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we should blow it up, but only the upper part of it, around VRS HQ and down to Godjenje IKM, that part. We'll have to go a little bit to the left. Yes. It's okay. But I would need it, I think, on this screen. On this screen it's not ready yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For marking the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the Court Usher, please. We have to wait a little moment because it has to be done technically, in a proper way. Mr. Janc, is this sufficient for the purpose of marking it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you able to mark the route that we've just seen in the video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I will start from the beginning, where we stopped and we have seen the area underneath. So I marked it with X, for example. I don't know if you can see it. It's inside the "Krivace IKM" circle, and this is on the point where they stopped. And then I will now go towards direction they were driving, so from this X towards the west. So this is the road, and they stopped here, in front of that building. You can see where they stopped. This is the 65th Protection Regiment Base. They stopped there. And from that point, they go down. And from this point down, I'm not sure which route exactly they go. But from the video you can see that General Mladic is referring to Maceha Hill, which is down here. I will circle it and put M inside it. And that's why I think they are travelling down here. And I will mark it with a dotted line because I'm not 100 per cent sure. This direction down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that what you learned from Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. He provided me with the GPS reading for the point which I marked with X, and then he told me about the route where they were driving down towards Maceha.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And this is what you've marked now?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, I would tender this marked map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The map with the markings will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 12th page of the Exhibit P104, the map marked by the witness in court, shall be assigned Exhibit P2241. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what I'd like to do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. This section of the road that the witness marked is not an asphalt road, and we did not see that the car rode along an un-asphalted road. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You may deal with that in your cross-examination, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is important in terms of admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You may deal with that in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the video that we saw, we can see General Mladic referring -- or saying, rather, something to the effect - and we have the subtitles - but something to the effect that, In the Podrinje, we thrashed the Turks. Now, the Podrinje, can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the area next to the Drina River, so where the Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves are at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
