utterances.text: He says, at roughly 2 minutes, 35 or so, into the video, that if it weren't for the Americans, or something to that effect, that the Turks would have disappeared long ago. And in the context of this video, does that refer to the Podrinje region that you've described?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise, but I have an objection again. The witness is talking about the authenticity of the road and the footage but not about the things that Mr. Vanderpuye is asking him about. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Maybe I can clarify it, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is the route that you indicated on the map in -- that we can see the car navigating down in the video -- in the area of the Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And in the context of the video, where General Mladic says that if it weren't for the Americans, that the Turks would have disappeared a long time ago, first, that occurs on the route that you've described, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And based on that, is that why you are saying that it relates to -- or are you saying that his statement that the Turks would have disappeared from these parts, or something to that effect, relates to the Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also indicated in the photograph -- I'm sorry, the map that you marked that they stopped, you said, at the 65th Protection Regiment. And in the video footage we can see that they do stop at around 4 minutes, 35 seconds, and General Mladic describes it, I think, as a battalion.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is one of the battalions of the 65th Protection Regiment Base -- Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how are you able to make that determination?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is coming out of the investigation itself, and we obtained this information from the witnesses we interviewed, that that was their base or one of their battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you identify for the Trial Chamber, based on the investigation, which battalion it would be, first, and, second, what the source is of that information? If it's confidential, let us know, obviously. But if you're able to do that, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might not be right regarding which battalion it is, but I think it is the 2nd Battalion, 2nd Motorised Battalion. And these information are coming from the commander of this regiment, Mr. Savcic, Milomir, who will be coming here and testify; also his deputy, Malinic, Zoran. Those are the two main sources, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you one other bit of footage from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, one question. You have used 65 ter 6580, under seal. Are you tendering it or did you already tender it? I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I haven't tendered it. I didn't intend to tender it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I just was informed that there might be a problem with two documents, 65 ter 5507, under seal, and one part of 65 ter 7388, under seal, two videos. And I would like to know if they are identical, or different, or different editions of the same; that would clarify the situation. If you need to go into private session for a clarification, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think I need to go into private session. 5507 is an un-subtitled version and a complete -- the complete footage which underlies 65 ter 7388. So 7388 is the only subtitled part of that video footage, the totality of which is 5507.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Registrar made a proposal, how to deal with the documents, and I need some further clarification. 65 ter 5507 is the same video-clip, under seal, as that part of 65 ter 7388, under seal, the part we have seen today. The first one, 5507, contains also a translation and a transcript. That means a transcript and the respective translation of the transcript, but perhaps not subtitles. We can't check that at the moment. Our proposal would be to take that video under seal from 7388 and put it on the same number 65 ter 5507 so that we can identify that part. And the other parts of 7388 then could be dealt with as public documents. I hope I could express myself understandably.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see. That seems to make a lot of sense. If I understand you correctly, it makes perfect sense. I just want to point out, though, that 5507, as it is now, contains much more footage than what's on 7388, but it seems to work out just fine anyway if we simply supplant what's on 5507 with the clip here. The only reason why I played 5507 to begin with was to place some context to the clip which is 7388. It's less material. But if that works out fine, then I think it's a great idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The first step, then, should be to withdraw the clip we have seen, the confidential one, from 7388 and to combine it with 5507. Then we will decide about admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. That is my application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This document will be received under seal. That means 65 ter 5507, including the confidential part of 7388.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 5507 shall be assigned Exhibit P2242, admitted under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- you are exceeding the time of two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm aware of that. I have one other clip --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- that I'd like to play. It's from 65 ter 7388. We can do this in open session. We'll need to play it from about 10:49. It's four minutes long.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I just make one correction when we still have this map on the screen, just a quick one?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because before, I wasn't sure regarding this route, and now I think, because the letters are really slow, I now would like to mark it again, just the second part of the route from the 65th Protection Regiment Base down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should have on the screen an unmarked version, and you should mark it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I have this unmarked version in front of me, and I will try to mark it. Actually, the Maceha Hill - I'll mark it again - is here, and I will put "M1." So they are going from 65th Protection down here, actually, down this road here. And then when Mladic is saying they are 300 metres away from the enemy line, that corresponds to his statement, because they are really, really close to the enemy line which is, in this case, this blue line. And Maceha Hill is here [indicates], so this should be the correct route from the 65th Protection down towards Godjenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If you could, just put an arrow so we can see the direction that they would be travelling on the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First part of the road is here, arrow, they're coming, arrow 1. And then the second part, they're coming down here, arrow number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I take it you replaced the dotted line you put on the first marked map by this line with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to tender this as well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 12th page of Exhibit P104, marked by the witness for the second time in court today, shall be assigned Exhibit P2243. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We'll need to go back to 65 ter 7388, and we'll play it from, yeah, just about here, 10.5 -- 10:50 through 14:15.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We've stopped at 14:14.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us about the provenance of this video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received this video -- I mean, the OTP received it in April of 2002 from an individual, a citizen of Serbia. His name is Petrusic, Jugoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What are you relying on for that information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information I obtained from the records in our database, in the OTP database, regarding the source of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: These records relate to -- or are they kept regularly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are in electronic format. You can access it in an electronic way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is there any requirement that you're aware of to make these records upon the receipt of evidence or other documents from various sources?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every time the investigator sees or obtains any evidence, it should be placed in Evidence Unit vault, accompanying with this kind of information, electronic information data.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this procedure -- is this a procedure that is routinely followed and required to be followed by investigators in the course or the context of handling evidence that's received from various sources?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you -- or can you recall the name of the investigator that received this material that's indicated in this electronic record that you consulted?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's Investigator Yves Roy. That's the one I believe, but I'm not 100 per cent sure right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. But you, I take it, are able to confirm that one way or another.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, can you state, for the record, in relation to the list of documents, what did we see between 10:5 and 10:50 -- 10:50 through 14:10?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. You're right, I overlooked that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're understood Mr. President's question. Could you please answer it, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's actually the footage of the first anniversary of the existence of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, which was officially formed on 12th of October, 1994. And this is what was going on one year later, so in October 1995. So the place of this celebration is Dragasevac, near Vlasenica, and this is based on the information provided to us and the testimony of Drazen Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you see that -- rather, is Drazen Erdemovic actually featured in this video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is featured, and he was also named in this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you just tell the Trial Chamber what is the relationship of the 10th Sabotage Detachment to the Main Staff? What is the relationship of that detachment to the location, Dragasevac, as you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of their platoons was situated in Dragasevac. The other one was in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. Vanderpuye is once again trying to use this witness not only for identification, but also to confirm contents and information that he already has from other sources. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm only trying to assist the Court to understand the video footage. I should point out something, though, which I think will be helpful, which is that you have, in the trial record, the testimony of Drazen Erdemovic, which I think you'll remember, and if not, you certainly can consult with respect to the events that are depicted in this video-tape. So I don't think that there's anything improper or untoward about asking Mr. Janc to explain what the relationship is between the Sabotage Detachment and the location where this footage purports to have been shot. And I think it's responsive to the question of authenticity. Clearly, if it was shot in Warsaw, that might indicate that it was not an authentic film. So it seems to me that it's appropriate and corresponds to the scope of Mr. Janc's testimony here today. I'm not sure if this is -- this hasn't been admitted, and so I would tender it for that purpose. I should point out, though, that there is footage that is not, as I understand it, subtitled that is already admitted in evidence in this case. That is the same footage, once again. So it's -- P234 and P235, under seal, correspond to this same footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if my recollection is correct, I think that this video footage, if not in its entirety, then at least in part, it was shown during the testimony of Witness Drazen Erdemovic, so all the questions being put to the witness by the Prosecutor have already been looked into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I remember very well that we have seen at least part of that footage. I would like to read out the witness summary provided by the OTP to the Defence and to the Chamber in this respect. I quote: "In addition to describing how the OTP obtained the video footage, Mr. Janc will explain the events which are captured in the videos and identify some of the relevant individuals recorded therein." In relation to this, what is your objection, if you take this into account?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we don't have any objections. Mr. Vanderpuye can proceed as he wishes, because all the objections are just pro forma, they're not being taken into account. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, they are taken into account. We are discussing the topic. I invited you to explain it further. If you don't want to do that, that's fine. We must have our second break now, and we will resume 20 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you indicated that you need two hours. You have, up to now, used two hours and thirty-three minutes. You should come to an end as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe I am at the end. I just wanted to make sure that I tendered the last video-clip that was shown from P2228, and I understand the Trial Chamber has some information with respect to the status of that exhibit. I also wanted to let the Trial Chamber know that while I was conducting the examination, I had mentioned, in private session, that the Office of the Prosecutor had received certain information that warranted proceeding in private session and also which was the basis for submitting these exhibits under seal, and I received information while I was in court, through e-mail, that those restrictions are not necessary. So those documents don't need to be under seal. That's 5507 and -- 65 ter 5507 and P2228 don't need to be under seal. And, further, to the extent that there's future use of those documents, there's no concern for displaying them publicly in e-court or discussing them publicly otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it the Chamber can lift the confidentiality of these two videos, these two documents, and of the transcript in private session of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have had two private sessions today, and that relates to both private sessions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the first one related to a protected witness, so I think not with respect to that. But the second one, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are correct. The Chamber will lift the confidentiality of the two videos, and the long part we dealt with these videos in private session may be public now. To clarify, the status of the two documents, 65 ter 5507 and P2228, I think now there is no need to combine the two confidential parts of that. They should remain as they are, as 65 ter 5507 and 65 ter 7388, which is marked for identification as P2228; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. The document 65 ter 5507 is now in evidence as P2242, and the other one is marked for identification, as we indicated earlier today, pending receiving the transcript and the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With that, I've concluded my direct examination of Mr. Janc on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just a short introduction. The Defence, before Mr. Tolimir commences his cross-examination, we just want to say that we'll be discussing two topics. The first one will be the videos that have just now been admitted into evidence. And tomorrow, after we finish our cross-examination on that issue, we will continue the cross-examination that was started about a year ago, and it is in relation with a report by Mr. Janc on the DNA analysis. We will inform the Chamber, of course, when we intend to move to the next -- to the second topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is there an agreement among the parties about this kind of procedure? Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do believe so, Mr. President. If you have had an opportunity to see the schedule for the week, you must have seen that Mr. Janc would be testifying about, first of all, topics that he had testified before, in the period of about more than a year ago. We will continue the cross-examination in relation to that. And the other part was something that was normally scheduled; namely, the topics that were discussed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have received the schedule for the witnesses for this week, and there is mentioning for tomorrow re. exhumations and cross-examination only. You are absolutely right. Thank you very much for that. Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, you may now commence your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. May God's peace reign in this house, and may God's will, not mine, be done in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to extend my greetings to Mr. Janc and wish him a welcome, and I would also like to ask him to answer several questions of mine. First of all, you were shown a video-recording dated 19th of July. On page 3, line 3, that's when it was admitted. And on page 518 [as interpreted], there was discussion about Mr. Wood, who told you all the information about VRS members who were present at the meeting -- who had been present at the meeting. That was on page 5, line 18. And this is my question: Have you ever seen Major Indjic personally? In other words, were you ever together with him, or is it that all that you know about him was derived from video materials and photos?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never seen him. I have never met him. All the information about him is, indeed, from the investigation, from this kind of material we have been watching today, which are the videos, different statements, and other documents on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Was General Tolimir present in the footage and was it clear that he was present at the meeting in Jela? Can he be seen in the footage about the meeting in Jela? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see you, General Tolimir, before the meeting, and we stopped the footage at the point where the camera caught you. And this is before the actual meeting or the signing of the agreement took place, so when we can see General -- I mean Mr. Wood still printing out the agreement. So at that point in time we can see you. But later on, during the meeting, the signing of the agreement itself, no, we cannot see yourself on the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Could you please tell us whether Mr. Tolimir can be clearly seen during the meeting or can we just see him somewhere in this Restaurant Jela because it's possible that this film was made at a different point in time? Have you seen any footage of Tolimir in Restaurant Jela, apart from what we've seen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This whole footage is going on inside Jela Restaurant. And when we can see you on this footage, this is inside Jela Restaurant. It's just before the actual meeting started with General Smith -- between General Smith and General Mladic. So where we can see the signing of agreement, we can't see you, but I can say that from Mladic's comments and Mladic's speeches and talkings [sic] during this conversation to General Smith, he's referring to you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. It is not important whether Tolimir was or was not present there for the purpose of my question, but I would just like to ask you whether one can see General Tolimir sitting together with Generals Mladic and Smith at the time when the agreement was signed. And, secondly, would it be logical for him to be there if he took part in the agreement preparations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this footage, we can't see yourself being -- sitting there, but it doesn't mean that you were not there. Actually, it's just perhaps the camera didn't catch you. But from the records, which is one of those being the actual report of Lieutenant-Colonel Baxter, it's obvious that you participated in this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Are you basing your testimony on written information, predominantly, and transcripts of General Mladic's words, or was the main source of recognition the video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them are important, and I have taken into consideration all of them. So if you put together all this information, there is no doubt that you were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. On page 12, line 4 and onwards, you were shown video footage of Restaurant Jela of 20th of July when you recognised General Milovanovic, and you will remember that. And my question to you is: Was General Tolimir in front of the Jela Restaurant on the 20th of July, 1995, or inside of it, and was he somewhere on the footage? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are not on the footage. And according to information, we have no information that you were -- that you participated in this -- on this occasion. So you were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Please tell us this now: Photographs and video footage, are they the basis of your testimony in relation to what transpired within Restaurant Jela, bearing in mind that you never got to see the Restaurant Jela because it was destroyed before you first visited the location where the restaurant had been? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is -- these footages are, indeed, very important because Jela Restaurant doesn't exist anymore, nowadays, so we cannot actually go there and check certain things. But not only the video itself, I would say, is the main source. In addition to that, we have several statements which the OTP obtained during the years which corroborate these facts that this was, indeed, happening there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As an investigator, are you testifying on the basis of what you've read and what you've seen in video footage or do you use something else as the basis of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it's a combination of everything, what I've seen on the footage itself, what was discussed there, and as well what I was able to read from the documents, statements, and different sources. So it's a combination of everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. On page 25 of the transcript, lines 10 and onward, a document P740 was introduced. It was shown to you as well. It's video footage of General Tolimir in civilian clothes. On page 27, Mr. Vanderpuye asked you whether that was a segment from a documentary called "Story about Avdo Palic," recorded for the television. On page 24, you confirmed that, and you added that it wasn't a continuous video footage, that it was edited material. Do you remember having said that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember being asked about this topic, yes, if this is continuation of the video or is it somehow edited.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us, have you seen the film which was used to edit in the materials containing General Tolimir into the documentary about Avdo Palic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The original video, which is actually shown on a television and filmed by a camera for this documentary, we never obtained. And let me clarify regarding editing issue. It's not that the OTP edited anything. What we have been watching today is just what is on the documentary itself. Everything what you can see on documentary have been presented here in this courtroom today. In addition to that, we also presented another video from another source, which we obtained from the BiH authorities, which actually corroborates the first one. So the OTP never edited anything into these videos. What we presented is actually what we obtained and was ever on these videos, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. And that video footage that you received from Bosnia and Herzegovina, is that continuous material or is it again edited material of different situations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same as previous ones so -- because it's coming from the same source. And when I'm referring to the editing, it might be, most probably, that the camera was filming not all the way along but at one point it stopped and the cameraman started filming again. That's one possible explanation. The other one would also be that when this film was -- or this footage was taken by a camera, that it was going all along, and when it was broadcasted on a TV, was edited by the television itself, and that's what we were able to obtain, only what was broadcasted on a television at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. On page 28, line 12, you spoke about this documentary on Avdo Palic, and you told us that, We met a director who referred us to the BH authorities, and we received from them a longer segment of the events, including a segment that encompasses events that took place on the 24th of July. And this is my question to you: Do you, first of all, remember saying this during the direct examination? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. I would just like to clarify, I never met the director. Our team was in contact with the director of this documentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. On page 28, you told us that it was sent to the Prosecutor, this longer footage of events, including footage of events recorded on the 24th of July where Tolimir can be seen wearing civilian clothes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, that what we received in March this year from the BiH authorities. And the segment which was on that video which we received we have also seen today in this courtroom. So that's all what they provided to us, the whole segment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you talk to other sources and ask them whether Tolimir was ever at the Boksanica Hill wearing civilian clothes, although his senior officer was next to him in a uniform? Did you ask them that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I never asked anyone regarding this particular issue, and I'm sure that nobody from our team so far never asked anyone about this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In the footage where Tolimir is wearing civilian clothes on Boksanica, did you notice, did you observe, there that General Mladic is saying goodbye to everyone there, Kusic and all the others, but not the person wearing civilian clothes? Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he also greets Hamdija Torlak, who is also in civilian clothes there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But did he say goodbye, did he greet, General Tolimir, as you say, who's wearing civilian clothes in the footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this cannot be seen from this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like for this footage to be shown, starting with 20:29. This is document P740. This is OTP evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. If we cannot play that today, we'll do it tomorrow, because then you will see images that we are discussing. My apologies to the Trial Chamber and the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is my following question: The segment -- the edited segment of the Radio and TV of Bosnia and Herzegovina can be seen in both P740 and also in document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't catch the other number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please repeat the number of the second document. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, P2240.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your question, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No question. We've just located the section of the video, if General Tolimir wants to see it or to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's very helpful. Thank you. Is it possible to play it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We are grateful for your assistance, due to the absence of the team member of Mr. Tolimir who is normally providing the video. Thank you for that. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to avoid watching the whole sequence, I would like to ask you to play only the last eight or nine seconds, where people are saying goodbye to each other. 20:29, and then we continue to 20:30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you observe -- did you see, now, General Mladic saying goodbye to Mr. Tolimir, and can you tell us whether he greeted or said goodbye to all the other participants in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have to admit I paid attention to this particular issue for my first time now, and I see from this video that he wanted to greet you but you didn't, for some reason, want to greet him. So -- at least it's my understanding, so -- but he greets all the others, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I gather, from the direction of the cross-examination, that General Tolimir disputes that this individual in the blue suit is him on the video. If that's his position, I would ask that he put his case to the witness to that effect, as is required under the Rules. And if it's not his position, then I don't know the reason that we're belabouring the point. In addition, if it's his position that the video is somehow forged or manipulated, I would ask that he put that to the witness as well, because I think that is important and also required under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, this is not my understanding. He was asking to interpret the situation of saying goodbye and shaking hands. That's my understanding. But you may comment on that if you want, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. I don't want to make any comments. Footage will talk for itself. I'm asking the witness to give his comments, and whatever his answers are, that will be relevant. Let me repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the segment of the film P740 that we have just seen, and in the segment of the film that bears number P2240, do they both contain edited segments received from the Sarajevo Television -- or, rather, received from the Bosnian government?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to trust you now regarding the numbers, P numbers, so that's my confusion right now, but if P740 is the one we've just seen and P2240 is the one -- the documentary of Avdo Palic, then my answer would be, yes, they are -- they have both this edited part in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, but it's just past 7.00. We must adjourn for the day and we should resume tomorrow, and then you may continue the questions about the editing of certain videos. And I assume that will take some more time, that you can't finish this topic today. Thank you for your understanding. We must adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow in the afternoon, 2.15, in this courtroom. We adjourn.
